name: Asa Sul
tagline: The classic superquadras, shaded and self-contained
description: Asa Sul is the southern wing of Brasília's Plano Piloto, laid out as superquadras: blocks of six-storey buildings on pilotis, set in mature tree cover with a commercial strip behind each one. Bakeries, gyms, bars and schools sit within a few minutes walk, which is rare in this city.
bestFor: Nomads who want the real Brasília experience with daily needs on foot
pros: The most genuinely walkable district in the city
Deep shade and green space between every block
Close to the centre, the metro and Parque da Cidade
cons: Rents are high for the size of the apartments
Buildings from the 1960s often need maintenance
Quiet at night, nightlife is spread out and needs a car

name: Asa Norte
tagline: The younger wing, students and cheaper superquadras
description: Asa Norte mirrors Asa Sul on the north side of the axis but skews younger, thanks to the University of Brasília campus on its edge. The same superquadra layout applies, with commercial strips full of cheap lunch spots and bars, and rents that sit a step below the southern wing.
bestFor: Budget-conscious nomads who still want the walkable superquadra layout
pros: Cheaper rent than Asa Sul for the same building type
University crowd keeps bars and cheap food busy
Metro and the main bus axis both serve it
cons: Blocks further north feel isolated and underserved
Fewer specialty cafes than Asa Sul or Sudoeste
Some commercial strips feel deserted after dark

name: Sudoeste
tagline: Newer buildings, great food and the safest streets
description: Sudoeste is a newer wing southwest of the centre, built in the 1990s with the superquadra logic but taller, better-maintained buildings. It has grown into the city's best small restaurant and cafe district, sits beside Parque da Cidade, and consistently rates as one of Brasília's safest areas.
bestFor: Remote workers who want a modern apartment, good coffee and a park nearby
pros: Newer buildings with better internet and lifts
Excellent restaurant and cafe strip on the commercial blocks
Parque da Cidade next door for running and cycling
cons: Among the most expensive rents in the Plano Piloto
Feels newer and less characterful than the original wings

name: Lago Sul
tagline: Lakeside houses, embassies and big gardens
description: Lago Sul spreads along the southern shore of Lake Paranoá, a district of low-density houses with gardens, embassy residences and lakeside clubs. There are no apartment blocks and few pavements, so daily life runs on a car, but you get water views, sunsets and quiet that the wings cannot match.
bestFor: Nomads with a car and a bigger budget who want space and lake access
pros: Houses with gardens and lake access
Quietest and greenest part of the city
Lakeside bars and clubs for sunset
cons: A car is mandatory, almost nothing is walkable
The most expensive rents in the Federal District
Services and shops are scattered and thin

name: Noroeste
tagline: The newest wing, glass towers and eco-planning
description: Noroeste is Brasília's most recent planned wing, northwest of Asa Norte, built from the 2010s onward with taller glass-and-white blocks, solar water heating and wide green corridors. Commercial strips are still filling in, but apartments are the newest in the city and Parque Burle Marx borders it.
bestFor: Nomads who prioritise a brand new apartment and reliable infrastructure
pros: Newest housing stock with the best fibre connections
Wide green corridors and Parque Burle Marx alongside
cons: Commercial blocks are still half empty, few restaurants
Feels unfinished and lacks street life
Expensive for a district with limited amenities
